title: Each reasoning skill has its element
statement: Teach and credit each reasoning skill by its element: one dimension evidenced on both sides for comparison, a mechanism for cause, a baseline for change, a qualifying move for complexity.
detail: An AP history course's design document has evidence perform a named function: in a causal answer it connects a development to an effect through a mechanism, in a comparison it addresses the same dimension for both cases, and in continuity and change the student names the baseline. It teaches complexity as moves, qualifying a claim by actor, region, timeframe or persistence, corroborating across different evidence, or modifying it for a counter case, and a response must earn the relationship rather than insert a phrase. It sets this against a predictable error: students and generators imitate rubric terms, so a sentence beginning 'Although' is not automatically complex and naming two events is not comparison. The design document has since been marked historical, and no outcome was measured.
against: The comparison procedures are still proposals: the Grade 4 and 5 document marks its additions as proposed and not yet signed off, open to being rewritten or rejected (`othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/pedagogy/modelling-moment-procedures-g4-g5.md`, lines 10-12), and the Grade 5 draft says its additions require explicit sign-off before merge (`grade3-reading/visual-findings-2026-09-07/review-readiness/curriculum-alignment/rebuild/unit1/PROCEDURE-PROPOSAL.md`, line 5, and its copy `othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/pedagogy/grade5-procedure-proposal.md`, line 5). The history course's design document is marked historical and superseded, and no outcome was measured (`grade3-reading/_archive/2026-08-13-consolidation/apush-corpus-hardening-20260731-tip.tar.gz`, member `apush/docs/BRAINLIFT.md`, line 5).

evidence.quote: The course models a reasoning chain in which evidence performs a named function. In a causal answer, each piece of evidence must connect a development to an effect through a mechanism. In comparison, evidence for both cases must address the same dimension. In continuity and change, the student must name the baseline against which change is judged.
compare the same dimension across two cases;

Complexity is not taught as a decorative concession. Students learn to qualify by actor, region, timeframe, or persistence; corroborate across different evidence; or modify a claim when a counter case changes its scope. A response must earn the relationship, not insert a phrase.

Students and generators can imitate rubric terms without performing the historical work. A sentence beginning "Although" is not automatically complex. Mentioning purpose is not sourcing. Naming two events is not comparison.
Do not label this CONNECT: pupils must construct two evidence-bearing sides on one dimension before explaining similarity or difference.
Read question: determine what comparison and explanation the question requires.
Name dimension: hold one meaningful dimension constant, such as response to other people's needs or what draws a character toward others.
Build each side: select evidence for both sides on that dimension. Reject a true but irrelevant detail or a comparison that changes dimensions halfway through.
Explain comparison: explain the shared pattern and/or meaningful difference; do not merely restate two quotations.
